summary: No blocking correctness, security or registry API regression found in the exact frozen core-only candidate. Approval is limited to the reviewed source contract and offline evidence; it is not production or live-data acceptance.
checkout_state_at_review: PARKED: provider_manager.py matches base; candidate test is absent from checkout; existing documentation changes left untouched.
prior_review_attempt: Prior service usage-limit interruption produced no completed report and is not treated as a negative code verdict.

contract_review.conclusion: Public providers dictionary and register/remove/get/list semantics are preserved. Replacement keeps normal dict insertion semantics, absent removal is a no-op, get returns the original instance or None. Registry methods now use the same RLock as fetch.

Full iterable is materialized before fetching. Empty names/chains, whitespace-only names, mixed non-string entries, repeated labels, scalar str/bytes, non-iterables and noncallable acceptance are rejected before any manager-controlled fetch. Priority iteration order is preserved.

Missing registrations are recorded and skipped; each fetched nonempty payload must receive literal True from provider validation and, if supplied, the consumer. Exceptions at fetch, size check, provider validation and consumer acceptance advance to the next name. First success stops the chain; exhaustion raises an explicit error with immutable ordered attempts.

Attempt reasons contain exception class names, not exception messages. Final exhaustion is raised after the except block, avoiding an implicit chain to the handled provider exception. Returned data is excluded from dataclass repr. Trusted configuration labels remain visible by design.

The shared per-manager RLock covers registry methods and the complete fetch/validate/consumer cycle. Existing concurrency tests cover two fetch callers and concurrent removal; independent probe additionally covers register/get/list while consumer acceptance is active.

Construction creates only a dict and RLock; no provider, session, credential, order, UI or network configuration is added. Fetch calls occur only for explicitly registered names supplied by the caller.

independent_probe.execution: Python314/python.exe -E -B -; candidate manager and base_provider loaded directly into an in-memory package; no source restore or probe file written.
independent_probe.guard: Audit hook rejected socket events, subprocess launches and file-write opens; none occurred.
independent_probe.result: All 5 probes passed. This independent bounded probe is separate from historical full/targeted/rollback counts; counts must not be added.

limits: This verdict applies only to the two exact hashes above and the stated core contract; any source change requires a new source-matched assessment.

Existing full405 and targeted34 are inspected historical executions with matching before/after hashes and text logs. They were not independently rerun. Historical rollback17 applies to the base, not the candidate.

Serialization is per manager and through its methods. Direct public-dict mutation, direct fetch calls on instances returned by get_provider, and sharing one instance across multiple managers are outside that guarantee.

The RLock permits same-thread reentrant callbacks; no callback recursion policy is added. Providers and callbacks must bound their own work and avoid cross-thread waits that require the same manager lock.
Provider requests and consumer callbacks execute synchronously while holding the lock. No total deadline, cancellation, worker shutdown or UI responsiveness guarantee is provided.
Only None and zero-length Sized payloads are intrinsically rejected; other semantic validity, iterator payloads, price age and provenance require appropriate provider and consumer validation.
Accepted payloads remain raw mutable objects; repr protection is not blanket log redaction and does not make payloads safe to serialize or publish.
Exception class names and trusted provider labels are intentionally visible; raw exception messages are excluded from manager-produced traces. Raw provider-side logging is outside this module.
The three registry concurrency probe outcomes rely on bounded event-based test scheduling plus source inspection, not an exhaustive concurrency proof.
